newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian schools empty as teachers vow more strikes.
newsitem.headline: Serbian schools empty as teachers vow more strikes.

text.p: Up to nine out of 10 schools across Serbia were closed on Tuesday as teachers' unions vowed to continue a strike which is paralysing the education system, despite government claims to have reached an agreement.
Teachers' representatives met on Tuesday to discuss how to further their protest, aimed at securing a pay rise that would effectively double their wages.
But the government has refused their demands, saying it would have to print 3.3 billion dinars to fund the pay rise which would lead to inflation and destabilise the exchange rate.
Economists say Serbia has virtually no foreign reserves and unofficial estimates say up to half the labour force is out of work.
While the negotiations and demands harden, children have been stuck at home for the best part of two months, with only a couple of days schooling since their winter holiday.
Unions say classes have been stopped in 1,300 to 1,800 out of 2,000 schools in Serbia, from pre-school to secondary, and teachers say they will continue striking until their demands are met.

The pledges come only days after the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition halted three months of street protests following government recognition of local election results. Zajedno says it will restart the protests if the government does not show its intention to free Serbia's heavily-controlled media.

Belgrade students are still protesting daily and say they will continue demonstrating until the government sacks the university rector and prosecutes those responsible for annulling the local election results.
